cards.title: Foreign key propagation across the procurement document hierarchy
cards.body:
Procurement transactions establish an unbroken relational hierarchy using yearly document identifiers across schemas.
fIndent captures departmental demand, which fRequestforQuotation references through IndentNo and IndentDate foreign keys.
Vendor bids recorded in fQuotation store RFQNo and VendorLocationId to preserve source commercial context.
fCS aggregates quote IDs, evaluates line item prices, and passes selected vendor attributes into fPurchaseOrder.
Purchase order detail rows retain RefDocType, RefDocNo, and ItemId to preserve full traceability back to the indent.
fGateEntry registers arriving shipments by linking to the purchase order number and vendor location master.
fGRN consumes GateEntryNo and PONo in header records, ensuring line items validate against authorized order balances.
This relational key propagation ensures complete lineage reporting from requisition through stores receipt.

cards.title: Line item status recalculation and balance consumption logic
cards.body:
Downstream document authorization decrements open balances on parent records through transactional cascades.
Authorizing fPurchaseOrder decrements BalanceQty and updates reserved demand on corresponding fIndent detail rows.
When fGateEntry references a purchase order, validation routines lock order lines against concurrent gate duplication.
Authorizing fGRN decrements remaining open order quantities and transitions PO line status to Closed upon complete receipt.
When full quantities across all lines are received, header status on fPurchaseOrder transitions to Completed.
If an unauthorized receipt note is edited or cancelled, cascade handlers restore parent purchase order balances immediately.
Status recalculations execute within atomic database transactions to ensure consistency between orders and receipts.
This synchronization prevents accidental over-ordering, duplicate gate entries, and conflicting stores receipts.

cards.title: Standardized document numbering and stored procedure architecture
cards.body:
Every document in the flow generates sequential identifiers through standardized numbering stored procedures.
Document number generation evaluates prefix, financial year, and division mapping parameters from system settings.
Header and detail operations execute through specialized stored procedures such as Purchase.PMPOSave and IGRNSave.
Lookup datasets and dependent dropdown filters populate via routines like Purchase.PMPOFillValues and IGRNFillValues.
Delete operations invoke cascade handlers like Purchase.PMPODelete to verify dependent child references before row removal.
Shared validation routines execute server-side within custom validation procedures prior to transaction commit.
Structured exception codes returned by backend procedures are translated into user notifications by the application layer.
This modular architecture ensures uniform transaction processing and auditing across all procurement stages.

cards.title: Multi-tier approval workflows and authorization group schemas
cards.body:
Procurement records transition across Initial, Release, and Authorized lifecycle states during processing.
Authorization groups enforce user tier limits configured in masterdata.mAuthorizationGroup and linked user tables.
Intermediate approvers record sign-offs in approval audit tables without changing document state to Authorized.
The document remains in Release status until all required approval hierarchy tiers complete their review.
Only the designated final approver can trigger the transition of DocumentStatus to Authorized in the database.
Authorized status fires database triggers that make header and detail rows immutable against direct updates.
Document amendments create linked records in amendment tables, preserving previous revisions for compliance audits.
This state machine guarantees that commercial commitments adhere strictly to enterprise financial delegation matrices.

cards.title: Interface mechanics between purchase receipt and general ledger posting
cards.body:
Receipt authorization executes dual updates across inventory ledger and financial staging tables simultaneously.
Stock posting increments physical on-hand quantities within the Inventory.IStockLedger table for accepted items.
Concurrently, Account Determination Rules (ARD) evaluate item sub groups to identify debit and clearing accounts.
Valued receipt lines invoke Inventory.IGRNFinancePosting to create journal entries and staging lines for accounts payable.
Staging records write to Finance schema tables, making quantities and values available for consumption by fPurchaseBill.
If inspection rejected quantities exist, quarantine stock ledgers isolate the material pending dispatch returns.
Rollback handlers ensure inventory additions and financial staging records commit synchronously within a single transaction.
This interface boundary guarantees that physical stock movements match financial balance sheet valuations.
